speaker: Brenda Okoro
cascadeSummary: Operationalizing the Mayor's Stabilization Fund disbursement approval with processing details and district equity checks. Addressing neighborhood coherence concerns via community outreach realignment.

statements.decision: Process month-five disbursements (7 households) and reset outreach targeting based on neighborhood need patterns
statements.quote: Seven more households stabilized this cycle brings us to fifty-two of two hundred eighty served. The queue behind them tells us where to reset outreach — Fruitvale signals require equal attention.
statements.fullStatement: The Mayor's approval of month-five Stabilization Fund disbursements clears seven households for relief this cycle, bringing us to fifty-two of two hundred eighty served to date. Processing these applications revealed two insights we're acting on: first, that our West Oakland outreach remains effective but under-represents Fruitvale applicants facing comparable displacement pressure. Second, that neighborhood coherence concerns in West Oakland, Fruitvale and East Oakland demand an operational response. We're resetting next-cycle outreach to balance district equity while maintaining current processing pace. Marcus Webb's team will present the adjusted plan at next week's operations review.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C103: Month-five disbursement executed (7 households, total 52). Outreach reset planned for district equity.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: C104 operations review - outreach reset implementation

statements.decision: Realign community development staff to address neighborhood coherence concerns in West Oakland, Fruitvale, East Oakland
statements.quote: Neighborhoods don't become incoherent overnight. The signals we're seeing in West Oakland, Fruitvale and East Oakland have operational solutions — starting with feet on the ground.
statements.fullStatement: The Mayor's task force announcement on neighborhood coherence aligns with what our field visits have shown: West Oakland, Fruitvale and East Oakland need more than programmatic solutions. My office is realigning two community development staffers to coordinate block-level outreach in these districts next cycle, supplementing the Mayor's task force work. This isn't new funding — it's operational prioritization of existing resources toward the neighborhoods showing the clearest stress signals. We'll measure impact through both Stabilization Fund application patterns and direct community feedback.
